Q: Alfresco ACS Java REST API Spring Boot Starter: 401 after OAuth2 token expiration during long running jobs A:

With client_credentials, the client should request a new access token before it expires. Rather than adding try/catch everywhere, use a centralized OAuth2 token manager or HTTP interceptor that automatically renews the token and retries once on a 401. Also check if a newer version of the Alfresco REST API starter includes improvements for token handling.

Q: Entra External ID workforce user flow shows “Sign up with GitHub” although GitHub is not configured A:

The “Sign up with GitHub” option may appear due to default social identity provider settings or cached user flow configuration in Entra External ID. Check the user flow identity providers section and remove/disable GitHub if it is not configured or required.

Q: Python rpg boss infinite attacking loop A:

import pygame

import random

import sys

pygame.init()

# Screen

SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT = 900, 650

screen = pygame.display.set_mode((SCREEN_WIDTH, SCREEN_HEIGHT))

pygame.display.set_caption("Boss MPC - Drakonar (Dragon-Snake Hybrid)")

# Colors

BLACK, WHITE, RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW = (0,0,0), (255,255,255), (255,0,0), (0,255,0), (0,100,255), (255,255,0)

DARK_GREEN = (0, 80, 0)

font = pygame.font.SysFont("Arial", 36)

small_font = pygame.font.SysFont("Arial", 24)

# Stats

player_hp = player_max_hp = 600

player_atk = 55

boss_hp = boss_max_hp = 1000

boss_name = "Drakonar - Dragon Snake Hybrid"

state = "start"

damage_popup = []

potions = 2

def draw_dragon_snake(x, y, hp):

\# Snake body coils

pygame.draw.ellipse(screen, DARK_GREEN, (x-80, y+80, 280, 90), 0)

pygame.draw.ellipse(screen, DARK_GREEN, (x+60, y+120, 220, 70), 0)



\# Dragon head

pygame.draw.polygon(screen, (34, 139, 34), \[(x+220, y+60), (x+320, y+30), (x+340, y+110)\])

\# Eyes

pygame.draw.circle(screen, RED, (x+270, y+55), 18)

pygame.draw.circle(screen, RED, (x+300, y+55), 18)

pygame.draw.circle(screen, WHITE, (x+273, y+52), 8)

pygame.draw.circle(screen, WHITE, (x+303, y+52), 8)



\# Fangs + Horns

pygame.draw.line(screen, WHITE, (x+325, y+85), (x+335, y+115), 6)

pygame.draw.line(screen, WHITE, (x+310, y+80), (x+318, y+110), 6)

pygame.draw.polygon(screen, (169,169,169), \[(x+240,y+35), (x+255,y+10), (x+265,y+35)\])



\# Wings

pygame.draw.polygon(screen, (0, 100, 0), \[(x+100,y+40), (x+40,y-40), (x+120,y+10)\])

pygame.draw.polygon(screen, (0, 100, 0), \[(x+180,y+40), (x+240,y-50), (x+200,y+15)\])



\# HP Bar

ratio = max(hp / boss_max_hp, 0)

pygame.draw.rect(screen, RED, (x-50, y-60, 400, 25))

pygame.draw.rect(screen, GREEN, (x-50, y-60, 400 \* ratio, 25))

hp_text = small_font.render(f"{boss_name} HP: {int(hp)}/1000", True, WHITE)

screen.blit(hp_text, (x-40, y-85))

def draw_player(x, y, hp):

pygame.draw.rect(screen, BLUE, (x, y, 90, 180))  # armor

pygame.draw.circle(screen, (255, 220, 180), (x+45, y-20), 35)  # head

pygame.draw.line(screen, WHITE, (x+70, y+120), (x+130, y+60), 12)  # sword

ratio = max(hp / player_max_hp, 0)

pygame.draw.rect(screen, RED, (x-10, y+220, 180, 25))

pygame.draw.rect(screen, GREEN, (x-10, y+220, 180 \* ratio, 25))

# Main Loop

clock = pygame.time.Clock()

running = True

while running:

screen.fill((10, 10, 30))



for event in pygame.event.get():

    if event.type == pygame.QUIT:

        running = False

        

    if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN and state == "fighting":

        if event.key == pygame.K_a:  # Normal Attack

            dmg = random.randint(45, 75)

            boss_hp -= dmg

            damage_popup.append({"text": str(dmg), "pos": \[520, 180\], "life": 40, "color": YELLOW})

            

            \# Boss counter

            if boss_hp \> 0:

                boss_dmg = random.randint(50, 85)

                player_hp -= boss_dmg

                damage_popup.append({"text": str(boss_dmg), "pos": \[120, 280\], "life": 40, "color": RED})

                

        elif event.key == pygame.K_s and player_hp \> 0:  # Special Attack

            dmg = random.randint(70, 110)

            boss_hp -= dmg

            damage_popup.append({"text": str(dmg), "pos": \[510, 170\], "life": 45, "color": (255, 215, 0)})

            

            if boss_hp \> 0:

                \# Boss Special Attacks

                special = random.choice(\["fire", "poison", "tail", "roar"\])

                if special == "fire":

                    player_hp -= 75

                    damage_popup.append({"text": "Fire Breath 75!", "pos": \[110, 290\], "life": 50, "color": RED})

                elif special == "poison":

                    player_hp -= 45

                    damage_popup.append({"text": "Poison 45!", "pos": \[110, 290\], "life": 50, "color": (0, 255, 100)})

                elif special == "tail":

                    player_hp -= 60

                    damage_popup.append({"text": "Tail Sweep 60!", "pos": \[110, 290\], "life": 45, "color": YELLOW})

                else:  # roar

                    player_hp -= 55

                    damage_popup.append({"text": "Dragon Roar 55!", "pos": \[110, 290\], "life": 45, "color": RED})

        

        elif event.key == pygame.K_p and potions \> 0:  # Potion

            heal = 120

            player_hp = min(player_max_hp, player_hp + heal)

            potions -= 1

            damage_popup.append({"text": f"+{heal} HP", "pos": \[120, 250\], "life": 40, "color": GREEN})



\# Draw

if state == "start":

    title = font.render("BOSS MPC", True, RED)

    subtitle = font.render("DRAGON-SNAKE HYBRID", True, (0, 255, 100))

    screen.blit(title, (320, 180))

    screen.blit(subtitle, (280, 240))

    screen.blit(small_font.render("Press SPACE to start battle", True, WHITE), (320, 380))

    if pygame.key.get_pressed()\[pygame.K_SPACE\]:

        state = "fighting"



elif state == "fighting":

    draw_dragon_snake(380, 120, boss_hp)

    draw_player(80, 280, player_hp)

    

    \# Instructions

    screen.blit(small_font.render("A = Attack    S = Special Attack    P = Potion (" + str(potions) + " left)", True, WHITE), (180, 580))

    

    \# Popups

    for popup in damage_popup\[:\]:

        txt = small_font.render(popup\["text"\], True, popup\["color"\])

        screen.blit(txt, popup\["pos"\])

        popup\["pos"\]\[1\] -= 1

        popup\["life"\] -= 1

        if popup\["life"\] \<= 0:

            damage_popup.remove(popup)

    

    if boss_hp \<= 0:

        state = "victory"

    if player_hp \<= 0:

        state = "defeat"



elif state == "victory":

    screen.blit(font.render("VICTORY! You slayed Drakonar!", True, GREEN), (200, 220))

    screen.blit(small_font.render("Press R to play again", True, WHITE), (350, 340))

elif state == "defeat":

    screen.blit(font.render("DEFEAT... Drakonar wins.", True, RED), (250, 220))

    screen.blit(small_font.render("Press R to try again", True, WHITE), (350, 340))



\# Restart

if state in \["victory", "defeat"\] and pygame.key.get_pressed()\[pygame.K_r\]:

    player_hp = player_max_hp

    boss_hp = boss_max_hp

    potions = 2

    damage_popup.clear()

    state = "fighting"



pygame.display.flip()

clock.tick(45)

pygame.quit()

sys.exit()

Q: c++ abstract class : pure virtual covariant return A:

I would like to return something that keep the polymorphic information but without the pointer/reference lifetime problem.

Dynamic polymorphism requires an allocation to return values. You can hide it with std::polymorphic (or a backport), but it is there.

Aside: constexpr does not mean executed at compile time, it means can be executed at compile time. A constexpr function called with runtime parameters executes at runtime. consteval means executed at compile time.

Q: How to get whether the OS is 32-bit or 64-bit by UNIX command or in C? A:

Original question:

How to know the bits of operating system in C or by some other way?

The correct way is to use some system API or command to get the architecture, like uname on Linux or GetNativeSystemInfo on Windows. The bitness values of the OS, the CPU and the application are 3 different things. Most architectures/OSes are backward compatible so they can run 16 or 32-bit programs without problem. A 16-bit application can run on a 32-bit OS on top of a 64-bit CPU for example

Comparing sizeof in C won't give you the OS or CPU's pointer size but the target architecture's pointer size, i.e. the app's bitness. A 32-bit program's pointer is still 32-bit regardless of which OS it runs on. And even on 64-bit architectures, some OSes may still use 32-bit pointers such as x32-abi or Arm64ilp32
